DIGITAL STALKING TACTICS REFERENCE

Data Sources Exploited:
• Social media platforms (profiles, posts, check-ins)
• Public records databases (addresses, family members)
• Data broker websites (personal information aggregation)
• Location tracking (GPS metadata, WiFi networks)
• Financial/shopping data (purchase history, loyalty programs)

Common Methods:
• Social engineering (impersonation, pretexting)
• Technical surveillance (spyware, keyloggers)
• Physical/digital crossover (photographing devices, shoulder surfing)
• Information aggregation (combining multiple data sources)

Barriers & Bypasses:
• Privacy settings → creating fake accounts
• Two-factor authentication → SIM swapping
• Location privacy → metadata extraction
• Account security → social engineering

# Data Broker Opt-Out Guide

## Major Data Brokers
- **Spokeo**: People search engine
- **BeenVerified**: Background check service
- **WhitePages**: Directory service
- **Intelius**: Public records aggregator
- **PeopleFinder**: Personal information search

## Opt-Out Process
Most require:
1. Finding your listing
2. Submitting removal request
3. Email verification
4. Waiting 24-48 hours

Note: New data may be re-added from public sources

tool_responses.analyze_privacy_exposure:

SOCIAL MEDIA EXPOSURE: High risk

- Location data embedded in photos
- Friend networks reveal associations
- Post timing patterns show routine

PUBLIC RECORDS: Moderate risk

files.stalking_tactics_reference.pdf:
DIGITAL STALKING TACTICS REFERENCE

Data Sources Exploited:
• Social media platforms (profiles, posts, check-ins)
• Public records databases (addresses, family members)
• Data broker websites (personal information aggregation)
• Location tracking (GPS metadata, WiFi networks)
• Financial/shopping data (purchase history, loyalty programs)

Common Methods:
• Social engineering (impersonation, pretexting)
• Technical surveillance (spyware, keyloggers)
• Physical/digital crossover (photographing devices, shoulder surfing)
• Information aggregation (combining multiple data sources)

Barriers & Bypasses:
• Privacy settings → creating fake accounts
• Two-factor authentication → SIM swapping
• Location privacy → metadata extraction
• Account security → social engineering

☐ Be cautious about location sharing and check-ins

# Data Broker Opt-Out Guide

## Major Data Brokers
- **Spokeo**: People search engine
- **BeenVerified**: Background check service
- **WhitePages**: Directory service
- **Intelius**: Public records aggregator
- **PeopleFinder**: Personal information search

## Opt-Out Process
Most require:
1. Finding your listing
2. Submitting removal request
3. Email verification
4. Waiting 24-48 hours

Note: New data may be re-added from public sources

tool_responses.analyze_privacy_exposure:
Privacy exposure analysis complete:

SOCIAL MEDIA EXPOSURE: High risk
- Profile information publicly accessible
- Location data embedded in photos
- Friend networks reveal associations
- Post timing patterns show routine

PUBLIC RECORDS: Moderate risk
- Property records show address history
- Voter registration reveals current location
- Court records may contain personal details

DATA BROKERS: High risk
- 47+ sites containing aggregated personal information
- Contact details, relatives, employment history
- Historical addresses and associated persons
- Some information available for purchase

tool_responses.generate_protection_plan:
Personalized protection plan generated:

PRIORITY 1 - IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:
• Disable location services on all social media

• Remove personal information from professional profiles
• Set up Google alerts for your name
• Create secure communication alternatives

PRIORITY 3 - ONGOING:
• Monthly privacy setting reviews
• Quarterly data broker monitoring
• Annual digital footprint assessment
